Selected project / 12

Payment Operations Control Layer

The context.

Payment businesses often operate across multiple providers, application boundaries, and operational teams. This work focuses on a control layer that helps connect those pieces through defined workflows, integration boundaries, and evidence-driven testing. The portfolio describes prototype and architecture contributions.

My contribution.

  1. Contribute to architecture and delivery of an operational control-layer prototype for payment workflows.
  2. Work on payout-network integration boundaries, API behavior, and web/worker coordination.
  3. Support workflow remediation, security boundaries, and automated acceptance checks.
  4. Connect transaction status and reconciliation concepts with operational visibility.
  5. Translate product and stakeholder needs into engineering scope and implementation priorities.

The result.

  • Prototype workflows and integration boundaries supported by automated verification.
  • A practical foundation for conversations across product, operations, and engineering.
A control layer earns its place by making the underlying systems easier to operate and explain.
